verdict: Sempra's profit jumped to $877M from $77M a year ago — mostly because last year's quarter was crushed by a $514M tax charge on a planned stake sale, while this year added a gain on selling Ecogas, partly offset by a $205M regulatory disallowance in California.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $0.12 a year ago, when a $514M held-for-sale tax charge hit earnings

kpis.label: Equity earnings
kpis.note: profit from stakes in other companies, mainly Texas utility Oncor, which set a record 33.3 GW peak demand

kpis.label: Capital invested
kpis.note: invested in utility infrastructure in the first nine months of 2026 — money spent on buildings and equipment

segments.name: Sempra California
segments.note: San Diego Gas & Electric and SoCalGas — regulated gas and electric utilities serving Southern California; the bulk of the company's sales.

segments.name: Sempra Infrastructure
segments.note: Energy infrastructure in Mexico and LNG export projects, including Port Arthur LNG — revenue fell as the Ecogas business was sold in August.

segments.name: Parent, other & eliminations
segments.note: Corporate items and sales between the company's own businesses, removed so revenue is not counted twice. Sempra Texas Utilities (the Oncor stake) reports no consolidated revenue — its profit arrives as equity earnings below.

opex.name: Operation & maintenance
opex.note: Day-to-day cost of running the gas and electric networks and the energy businesses.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of pipes, wires and plants over their working lives — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: Franchise fees & other taxes
opex.note: Franchise fees and taxes other than income tax.

opex.name: Regulatory disallowances
opex.note: Costs California regulators disallowed from past years after proposed decisions in the 2024 rate case — a one-off charge this quarter.

otherDetail: Net other income of $9M combines a $214M gain on sales (including the sale of Ecogas in Mexico), $58M of other income and $35M of interest income, minus $298M of interest expense.
footerNote: Consolidated net income was $1,114M. The $877M shown is earnings attributable to common shares, after $231M attributable to noncontrolling interests and $6M of subsidiary preferred deemed dividends. The equity line of $431M is $668M of equity earnings (mainly Oncor) minus those $237M of attributions.

takeaways.title: The year-ago comparison does the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS rose from $0.12 to $1.34, but a year ago earnings carried a $514M tax charge for classifying Sempra Infrastructure Partners as held for sale. Adjusted EPS, which strips these items out, rose more modestly from $1.11 to $1.40.

takeaways.title: California disallowance bites
takeaways.text: Regulators' proposed decisions in the 2024 rate case produced a $205M pre-tax disallowance charge ($149M after tax) at the California utilities — a reminder that regulated returns depend on regulatory outcomes.

takeaways.title: Texas demand keeps setting records
takeaways.text: Oncor, Sempra's Texas utility stake, hit an all-time peak demand of 33.3 GW, up 6% on last year's record, and now expects its next five-year capital plan to rise about 20% to keep up with load growth.

oneTimers: $205M pre-tax regulatory disallowance charge at Sempra California ($149M after tax) from proposed decisions in the 2024 General Rate Case.
Gain on the sale of Ecogas in Mexico — $97M after tax (part of $214M of pre-tax gains on sales).
$65M favorable impact from foreign currency and inflation on monetary positions in Mexico, and $67M of net unrealized losses on commodity derivatives.
A year ago, earnings included a $514M tax charge from classifying Sempra Infrastructure Partners as held for sale — the main reason GAAP profit looks so much higher this year.
